text:
Pittsburgh's season has turned into a trade-deadline countdown in November. At 8-15-2 the Penguins are near the bottom of the East, and the rumor mill has Erik Karlsson and Rickard Rakell on their way out (Markerzone relayed beat reporter Josh Yohe saying both are about to be traded), Evgeni Malkin linked to Minnesota, and Sidney Crosby fielding questions about his future in the last year of his contract.

The frustrating part for Dan Muse is that the record is worse than the team. Our numbers say Pittsburgh has earned about 25 points on its chances and has 18, the second-biggest gap in the league. The Penguins get 52% of the expected goals at five on five, but they have scored about seven fewer goals than their chances deserve, the power play generates little, and Arturs Silovs is 0-5-0 with an .845 save percentage over his last five starts.

There is still plenty to like on a given night. Malkin came back this week with two power-play points and passed Bryan Trottier for 19th on the NHL's career points list. The Crosby, Rakell and Tommy Novak line has 53% of the expected goals, and the energy line of Connor Dewar, Blake Lizotte and Nick Robertson has quietly outscored opponents 4-1. Karlsson and Spencer Stastney have been outscored 13-6.

Our numbers give Pittsburgh a 7% chance at the playoffs. What we'd watch: the next few weeks of the trade market, because the decisions about Karlsson, Rakell and Malkin will shape this team more than the standings will.
